title: Celery producer witch rpc backend cannot fetch results when rabbitmq is restarted

# Steps to Reproduce 1. Start the worker and import the tasks add. 1. Reboot the broker. 1. Call the task add and try to get the result. Example: ``` # Start python and rabbitmq containers docker-compose up -d # In one shell, start the worker docker-compose exec python celery -A tasks worker --loglevel=DEBUG # In another shell, run pyton interpreter docker-compose exec python python # Import add task and run it first for test >>> from tasks import add >>> add.delay(15,32).get() ``` If the setup is OK, reboot the broker and wait for the worker to reconnect then try to call the add task in the same shell as previous call. ``` # Reboot broker docker-compose restart rabbitmq # In previous python shell, try to call the add task again. >>> add.delay(15,32).get() ```

## Minimally Reproducible Test Case

```python from celery import Celery app = Celery('tasks', broker='pyamqp://guest:guest@rabbitmq/', backend='rpc://') @app.task def add(x, y): return x + y ```

# Expected Behavior When the broker is rebooted, the worker and the producer should reconnect automatically and keep producing and consuming message. # Actual Behavior In one hand, when the broker is rebooted, the worker reconnects automatically and keep consuming message as expected. But on the other hand, for the producer, when the broker is rebooted, tasks are sent and the worker can consume them. But results are never pulled out. An `ConnectionResetError` exception is raised by the producer when the `task.get`method is called.
